full_text:
In the bustling Anatolian town of Akşehir, where donkey carts rattled through the spice bazaar and tea glasses clinked under the plane trees, lived Mulla Nasruddin. One afternoon, When an arrogant governor brought his prized hunting hound into court to intimidate the judge, Nasruddin brought his gray donkey right into the courtroom and tied it to the judge's.... The local folk, who never missed an opportunity to hear the Mulla’s unexpected pronouncements, quickly formed an expectant circle around him, stroking their beards and whispering among themselves.

Seeing everyone staring at him with grave expressions, Nasruddin adjusted his voluminous turban with theatrical dignity. A crowd of curious onlookers gathered in a circle, eagerly anticipating how the Mulla would resolve the impossible dilemma. Rather than offering a conventional, boring answer that any dry scholar might recite, the Mulla approached the problem from an angle that no one in the village had ever dreamed possible.

With effortless timing and a completely straight face, Nasruddin delivered his masterstroke: With deadpan gravity and a twinkle in his eye, Nasruddin delivered his unforgettable verdict.  The entire square erupted into bewildered chuckles and hearty laughter, leaving the bewildered questioners shaking their heads in admiration, proving that true justice treats all parties without fear of power or pretense.
moral: True justice treats all parties without fear of power or pretense.
